security_audit.summary: The audit reviewed all 175 static findings. One medium-risk issue is confirmed because the template generator can overwrite any writable path supplied through its output argument. All other alerts are benign PyTorch calls, Markdown formatting, dataset cache paths, dictionary keys, imports, or official URLs.

remediation.issue: Template generation can overwrite arbitrary writable files.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict output to the working directory, reject existing files by default, and require an explicit force option for replacement.

static_findings.snippet: 2. **Citation networks**: Planetoid datasets are perfect for node classification
PyG represents graphs using the `torch_geometric.data.Data` class with these key attributes:
- **`data.edge_index`**: Graph connectivity in COO format `[2, num_edges]`
- **`data.y`**: Target labels for nodes or graphs
Edges are stored in COO (coordinate) format as a `[2, num_edges]` tensor:
- A `batch` vector maps each node to its source graph
- **`message()`**: Constructs messages from source to target nodes

content.user_title: Build Graph Neural Networks with PyTorch Geometric
content.value_statement: Graph learning projects require specialized data structures, layers, sampling, and evaluation workflows. This skill provides PyTorch Geometric guidance, references, templates, visualization, and benchmarking utilities.
actual_capabilities: Explains Data objects, edge indices, batching, custom datasets, and CSV graph loading.
Covers GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GIN, message passing, pooling, and normalization choices.
Provides node and graph classification training loops with evaluation and GPU placement patterns.
Covers heterogeneous graphs, neighbor sampling, transforms, explainability, and model persistence.
Generates editable Python templates for supported node and graph classification models.
Benchmarks supported models and visualizes graph structure, degree distributions, and dataset statistics.
limitations: It does not install PyTorch Geometric or verify binary compatibility automatically.
Bundled templates cover selected architectures and require adaptation for custom data and production workloads.
Benchmark results depend on downloaded datasets, hardware, package versions, seeds, and chosen hyperparameters.
The scripts do not provide distributed training, experiment tracking, deployment, or production security controls.

use_cases.title: Learn graph modeling fundamentals
use_cases.description: Create Data objects, understand edge indices, and train a first node classifier with clear tensor and evaluation guidance.

use_cases.title: Prototype scalable GNN workflows
use_cases.description: Compare architectures, apply transforms, use neighbor sampling, and benchmark models before integrating them into a larger project.

use_cases.title: Model scientific graph data
use_cases.description: Select datasets, layers, pooling, and heterogeneous graph patterns for molecular, biological, spatial, or relational research.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic PyG graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Represent my node features and edge list as a PyTorch Geometric Data object. Explain tensor shapes and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build a node classifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GCN node classification workflow for [dataset]. Include splits, preprocessing, training, validation, testing, and metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Scale graph training
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my [model] for a graph with [node count] nodes. Choose neighbor sampling, batch settings, device handling, and memory controls.

prompt_templates.title: Design a heterogeneous pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a heterogeneous GNN for [node types], [edge types], and [target]. Compare conversion and HeteroConv, then define evaluation and explainability.

output_examples.input: Choose a model for citation network node classification.
output: Recommendation: use GCN for a clear baseline, then test GAT when neighbor importance may vary.
Workflow: normalize features, use provided masks, track validation accuracy, and report the selected test result.
Checks: confirm edge direction, class balance, isolated nodes, and feature dimensions.

output_examples.input: Plan a fair comparison of GCN, GAT, and GraphSAGE.
output: Use identical data splits, epoch budgets, seeds, hidden dimensions, and evaluation metrics.
Report accuracy and training time across repeated runs with mean and variation.
Record hardware, package versions, and memory limits so the comparison can be reproduced.
Represent users and items as separate node types with typed interaction edges.
Select relation-specific message passing, define negative samples, and prevent temporal leakage.
Evaluate ranking quality by user segment and inspect explanations for influential relations.

best_practices: Validate feature shapes, edge indices, labels, masks, and graph direction before training.
Use fixed splits and seeds, then report repeated runs with hardware and package versions.
Start with a simple baseline before adding attention, deeper layers, sampling, or heterogeneous relations.
anti_patterns: Do not evaluate on the test split while selecting models or hyperparameters.
Do not load a full large graph onto one device when neighbor sampling is required.
Do not compare architectures with different data splits, preprocessing, or training budgets.

faq.question: Does this skill install PyTorch Geometric?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation commands, but users must run them and select versions compatible with their PyTorch and accelerator setup.

faq.question: Which tasks are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance covers node classification, graph classification, link prediction, heterogeneous graphs, molecular modeling, geometric data, and large-graph sampling.

faq.question: Can it generate complete training code?
faq.answer: Yes, for selected GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, and GIN examples. Generated templates still require review and adaptation.

faq.question: Does it support custom datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Data objects, in-memory and disk-backed datasets, CSV loading, transforms, and split construction.

faq.question: Can it benchmark models?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled benchmark compares supported architectures on common node or graph datasets and summarizes accuracy and training time.

faq.question: Can it visualize graphs?
faq.answer: Yes. The visualization utility can render graph structure, labels, attributes, degree distributions, and summary statistics for supported datasets.
